subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Should message_tool_only visible-reply guidance be removed from cache-visible OpenAI/Codex tool schemas and system/instructions prefixes and carried only in late turn context?
rationale: The cache contract favors stable schemas and instructions, but the current conditional hint is part of the visible-reply steering contract, so automation should not choose the final prompt boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Move Volatile Guidance Late
options.body: Make the message tool description and OpenAI/Codex instructions stable, inject turn-specific delivery guidance after the stable prefix, and require live cache plus delivery proof.

options.title: Keep Schema Steering
options.body: Preserve the conditional tool/system prompt guidance and accept the documented OpenAI/Codex prompt-cache cost for stronger visible-reply steering.

options.title: Wait For Fresh Live Telemetry
options.body: Hold implementation until maintainers collect current-main provider traces identifying the remaining churn bytes after the room-event candidate lands or is rejected.

recommendation.title: Move Volatile Guidance Late
recommendation.body: Make the message tool description and OpenAI/Codex instructions stable, inject turn-specific delivery guidance after the stable prefix, and require live cache plus delivery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved implementation touches the prompt/tool construction and source-reply mode threading paths where recent reachable history points most strongly to this owner.
